test_title: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper (Held On: 12th September 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Pipe P can fill a tank in 8 hours, pipe Q in 12 hours, and pipe R can empty it in 6 hours. All three pipes are opened together and they operate for 1 hour after that pipe R is closed. How much additional time will it take to completely fill the tank after that?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity (LCM of 8, 12, 6) = 24 units.

Efficiencies: P = 3, Q = 2, R = −4 (Negative as it empties).

Combined work in 1 hour (P + Q + R) = 3 + 2 − 4 = 1 unit.

Remaining work to fill = 24 − 1 = 23 units.

Additional time for P and Q = 23 ÷ (3 + 2) = 23 ÷ 5 = 4(3/5) hours.

**&there4$ The correct answer is 4(3/5) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P = 8 hours, Q = 12 hours, R = 6 hours (Outlet pipe).

**Formula Used:**

Total Capacity = Efficiency × Time; Net Efficiency = Σ Individual Efficiencies.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P (Fill)
 8
 24 units
 +3
 
 

 Q (Fill)
 12

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency of (P + Q + R) = 3 + 2 − 4 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Tank filled in 1 hour = 1 × 1 = 1 unit

⇒ Remaining capacity = 24 − 1 = 23 units

⇒ After closing pipe R, net efficiency (P + Q) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/hr

⇒ Additional time required = 23 ÷ 5 = 4(3/5) hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4(3/5) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Convention

Filling pipes (Inlets) are treated as positive work, while emptying pipes (Outlets) are treated as negative work.

Net Work Done

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, then net work in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y) units.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the task. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.
